notes: The parts are the same as in step 1. Nothing was added or dropped.
The manual excerpt doesn't say which Pi pins to use. I picked the usual ones for a PIR sensor: VCC to pin 2 (5V), OUT to pin 7 (GPIO4) and GND to pin 6 (GND).
The PIR runs on 4.5-20 V, so it gets 5 V. Its OUT signal is 3.3 V logic, so it is safe for the Pi's GPIO input.
I assumed the Pi is a Raspberry Pi 4 with a 40-pin header, and that the sensor is wired straight to the Pi with three jumper wires and no breadboard.
Wire colours are assumed: red for power, yellow for signal and black for ground.
The sensor's pin order (VCC, OUT, GND) follows the catalogue card. Check it against the markings on the module, because some PIR modules print the pins in a different order.
